public_payload.normalized_proposition: Even assuming a 75% token gross margin, a subscriber using 25% of their rate limit yields at best a -25% gross margin.
conditions: assuming a 75% gross margin on tokens

statement.excerpt: That’s right folks. With the current subsidies, all it takes for a user to have a gross margin of at best negative 25% is for them to use as little as 25% of their rate limit.

from_speaker: gross margin of at best negative 25%
our_interpretation: This is a claim about the stated model's arithmetic, not a disclosure of actual company margins.
A 75% API gross margin implies serving costs equal to 25% of API-price-equivalent consumption.
At best means that the highest modeled subscription margin among the tested tiers is no greater than -25%.
Utilization is assumed to scale API-equivalent consumption proportionally, with a constant workload mix.
The target is the current month through publication, June 1–15, 2026.
criteria.support_condition: Applying the assumed serving-cost ratio to 25% utilization produces margins of -25% or lower across the cited tiers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Under the same model and inputs, at least one cited tier produces a margin above -25% at 25% utilization.
